t:
(a) 
Section 1 of article VI of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1947 (D.C. Code, sec. 47–2501a) is amended to read as follows:


“Section 1. There are authorized to be appropriated, as the annual payment by the United States toward defraying the expenses of the government of the District of Columbia, not to exceed $173,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972, and not to exceed $178,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1973, and for each fiscal year thereafter. Sums appropriated under this section shall be credited to the general fund of the District of Columbia.”



 
    (b)

        (1) 
In addition to the amount authorized to be appropriated under section 1 of Article VI of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1947 (D.C. Code, sec. 47–2501a) for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972, there is authorized to be appropriated to the District of Columbia for such fiscal year not to exceed $6,000,000 which may only be used in such fiscal year to pay officers and employees of the District of Columbia increased compensation which is required by comparability adjustments made on or after January 1, 1972, in the rates of pay of statutory pay systems (as defined in section 5301(c) of title 5, United States Code), based on the 1971 Bureau of Labor Statistics survey.
 
        (2) 
In addition to the amount authorized to be appropriated under section 1 of Article VI of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1947 (D.C. Code, sec. 47-2501a) for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1973, and for each fiscal year thereafter, there is authorized to be appropriated to the District of Columbia not to exceed $12,000,000 for each such fiscal year which may only be used to pay officers and employees of the District of Columbia increased compensation which is required by comparability adjustments made on or after January 1, 1972, in the rates of pay or statutory pay systems (as defined in section 5301(c) of title 5, United States Code), based on the 1971 Bureau of Labor Statistics survey.

fable.w: The section only authorizes appropriations for the federal payment to the District of Columbia and for pay increases for District employees. The tempting reading is that the District of Columbia's involvement as a local government counts as participation, but it is only the recipient of funds. Nothing here provides for consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, as the annual payment by the United States toward defraying the expenses of the government of the District of Columbia

opus.w: This section only authorizes appropriations: the annual federal payment to the District of Columbia and extra sums for employee pay raises. It might look like outside involvement because the District is a non-federal government that receives the money. But receiving funds is not consulting on a federal decision. The BLS survey it relies on is a federal product, and the section creates no hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation duty or right to sue.
opus.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, as the annual payment by the United States toward defraying the expenses of the government of the District of Columbia
opus.b:
I'd label this **No**. The section only authorizes money: it sets the annual federal payment to the District of Columbia and adds sums for pay raises for D.C. employees.

One possible misreading: the District of Columbia is a non-federal government receiving federal money, and the pay raises rest on a Bureau of Labor Statistics survey. Neither counts as participation. Receiving appropriated funds is not consulting on a federal decision, and the survey comes from a federal agency, so it stays inside the government.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations for the District of Columbia to pay its employees based on comparability adjustments derived from a Bureau of Labor Statistics survey. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the general public, states, or tribes) before making a decision. The reference to the BLS survey is a factual basis for calculation, not a participatory process involving outside stakeholders in the decision-making itself.
qwen_chat.s: there is authorized to be appropriated to the District of Columbia for such fiscal year not to exceed $6,000,000 which may only be used in such fiscal year to pay officers and employees of the District of Columbia increased compensation which is required by comparability adjustments made on or after January 1, 1972, in the rates of pay of statutory pay systems (as defined in section 5301(c) of title 5, United States Code), based on the 1971 Bureau of Labor Statistics survey.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to the "Bureau of Labor Statistics survey" implies participation because it involves data collection from the public or private sector. However, the statute itself does not mandate a process for public consultation, comment, or coordination; it merely uses existing survey data as a baseline for calculating federal appropriations for DC employee salaries. The actors involved in the decision-making (Congress appropriating funds, the District of Columbia paying employees) are either inside the government or the mechanism is purely administrative/financial based on pre-existing data, not interactive participation.
